summary: Initial discovery on reliability and incident tolerance. Arcturus is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a customer-facing inference product with strict latency SLOs and regulatory constraints. topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-10-20 15:00 PT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Lena Park, Omar Singh (Redwood); Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Priya Rao, Samir Patel (Arcturus AI)

Summary (auto): discovery focused on reliability, fallback and multi-region routing - uses plain language and some acronyms; transcription has occasional mismatches.

[00:00] Lena (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro - i'm Lena from Redwood, Omar is our solutions engineer. who wants to kick off on the Arcturus side?
[00:12] Maya (Customer): hi, Maya here. thanks. We run a customer-facing inference product - low latency chat and recommendation calls - traffic is global. main concerns are: if a region degrades, how quickly do we failover? and also how do we keep predictable cost.
[00:25] Omar (SE): Great, thanks. high level: Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. we do routing by policy - you can prefer latency or cost, and set fallback chains. e.g., if primary region latency spikes, auto-route to a secondary region or to a compatible model variant.
[00:40] Diego (SRE): what's the observable failover time? like detection + route switch? we need < 1 minute ideally, and a hard requirement of under 2 minutes for customer SLAs.
[00:52] Omar: detection depends on health checks and our circuit breaker, typically we see detection in 10-30s. route propagation and connection warmup to a new region... if you have Dedicated reserved capacity in that region it's much faster - we're talking 10-20s average extra. With Hosted, cold-start to a new region can add 30-90s depending on model size. So design pattern is keep warm pools or dedicate capacity for fast failover.
[01:18] Maya: ok that matches my expectations. We were thinking about using Hosted for simplicity but keep Dedicated in key regions to meet the SLA. is that a common pattern?
[01:28] Lena: yes very common - hybrid. many customers keep dedicated for core regions with predictable traffic and use Hosted for global burst and edge. That also gives you fallback diversity across model variants.
[01:40] Priya (Security): quick sec - around data control: in failover cases does data transit regions? we have regulatory rules for residency and encryption.
[01:49] Omar: good callout. by default requests route to the region you select; if you enable multi-region fallback we can configure whether payloads are allowed to cross boundaries. Private and Dedicated give you VPC options and customer-managed KMS. we also provide audit logs and retention controls.
[02:05] Priya: For KMS, do you integrate with our HSM or only cloud KMS?
[02:10] Omar: we support cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and also HSM via standard keywrap patterns - we'll share the KMS/HSM integration notes.
[02:18] Samir (PM): curious about fallback policy granularity - can we say go to quantized 4-bit model variant first, then to smaller architecture, then region?
[02:28] Omar: yes, fallback chains are policy driven. typical chain: primary model (full float, high perf) -> quantized variant (lower cost, slightly diff output) -> smaller model family -> secondary region. You can also configure quality thresholds and circuit breakers if quality drops below a threshold.
[02:46] Diego: interesting. what about cached responses or local edge cache? we use a lot of prefix caching and some long lived session KV. if a region fails, how do you restore KV cache semantics?
[02:58] Omar: we do prefix and kv cache at the instance level - cross-region cache is eventual. recommended pattern: keep short TTLs for critical cached tokens and replicate important state to a shared cache if you need immediate consistency - or keep session affinity in dedicated pools. we'll put notes in the architecture guide.
[03:15] Maya: SLA targets - what SLAs do you offer for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[03:20] Lena: Hosted: best-effort public SLA, usually no contractual 99.99 for lower tiers, but we offer 99.9% for pro customers; Dedicated: contractual SLA (e.g., 99.95% uptime and latency targets per route) with reserved capacity. Private: enterprise SLA with higher uptime and on-prem options. we can share exact SLA language.
[03:40] Diego: for latency SLO - our product needs p95 < 350ms for chat in the US, and p99 < 1s. can you meet that?
[03:49] Omar: yes on Dedicated in-region with warm pools, that's achievable. on Hosted it depends on model size; for large models p95 might exceed that unless we do ak--- (audio?) quantization or smaller variants. we also recommend batching and prefix caching for throughput.
[04:05] Priya: Do you provide tracing hooks and per-request IDs? we need full audit linkability.
[04:10] Lena: yes, per-request tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and audit logs are available. we also support SSO/SAML and RBAC for access control.
[04:19] Maya: can we do canary rollouts and automatic fallback if a new model fails quality evals?
[04:24] Omar: absolutely. Redwood Console supports rollouts (canary, A/B), auto-roll back on regression metrics, and automatic fallback to previous model. We also integrate eval sets to trigger alerts.
[04:36] Diego: how do you measure model quality differences when failing over to a quantized model? we care about hallucination increases.
[04:43] Omar: we surface quality deltas using evals tied to production prompt sets; you can set thresholds for acceptable degradation. For hallucination we surface confidence heuristics and you can route only non-critical traffic to quantized variants.
[04:58] Samir: what's the expected cost delta if we keep dedicated warm pools in two regions vs Hosted-only? rough numbers help.
[05:05] Lena: rough order: dedicated reserve can be 3-5x the unit cost vs cold-hosted but gives predictable latency; Hosted has lower base cost but higher variance and potential egress/cold start costs. we'll send a pricing scenario for your traffic profile.
[05:18] Maya: Another question: during incident recovery, do you support gradual traffic shifting vs all-at-once? we prefer gradual to monitor quality.
[05:26] Omar: yes weighted traffic shifting with canary ramp and automated rollback; you can do small steps and monitor both latency and quality signals.
[05:34] Priya: about logs - retention and export - can we push logs to our SIEM and have customer-controlled retention?
[05:40] Lena: yes push to S3/BigQuery/Customer SIEM; retention configurable in Private/Dedicated; Hosted has standard retention but enterprise plans extend retention.
[05:49] Diego: are there runbooks or playbooks for incidents you share?
[05:52] Omar: we have a runbook library; we'll share a runbook template for region failover, plus recommended alert thresholds.
[06:00] (small crosstalk)
[06:05] Maya: ok this is helpful. Can we walk through a concrete failure scenario? say us-east suffers a network partition - what happens step by step?
[06:15] Omar: detection from health checks -> circuit breaker trips -> traffic reroutes to secondary region or model variant per policy; if you have Dedicated in secondary region with warm pools the target latency is within 20-30s; if no warm pools, fallback to quantized/smaller model in same region or route to Hosted in another region, which can take 30-90s. logs and tracing flag the change; automatic rollback after recovery.
[06:40] Diego: do you support multi-cloud region failover? we run primary on AWS but want GCP as secondary.
[06:46] Omar: yes we support multi-cloud routing; must consider egress and data residency constraints - we'll show config options to disallow cross-cloud data movement if needed.
[06:58] Priya: what's the longest window you'd expect for model state rehydration in a cold region?
[07:04] Omar: depends on model size - small models a few seconds, large LLMs (multiple hundred GB) could need minutes to warm; so again warm pools for mission-critical regions.
[07:15] Maya: does Redwood have an SLA credit model? if you miss 99.95, how do credits work?
[07:22] Lena: yes standard SLA credits in contract; formula based on downtime percentage. we'll share the legal SLA text.
[07:30] Samir: any gotchas with sticky sessions and KV cache if routed mid-session?
[07:36] Omar: session affinity helps, but if you route mid-session some KV entries may not be available until cache warms; recommended to replicate critical session state or keep session pinned to dedicated pool.
[07:48] (noise, mis-transcription)
[07:52] Diego: last thing - how often do you run failover drills with customers?
[07:56] Lena: we run joint DR drills on request; for Dedicated+Private customers we do annual or quarterly drills depending on contract. good practice to do a staged failover test before production cutover.
[08:08] Maya: ok next steps then - we want the security docs, pricing, and the staging failover test.
[08:15] Lena: perfect. Omar will lead the staging test and we'll follow up. Thanks everyone.
[08:20] (meeting ends)
